title: Definition - Appellate Tribunal
clause_text: "Appellate Tribunal" means the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal established under section 14 of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
plain_english_summary: Defines the Appellate Tribunal as TDSAT, which hears appeals under this Act.

title: Definition - Board
clause_text: "Board" means the Data Protection Board of India established by the Central Government under section 18.
plain_english_summary: Defines Board as the Data Protection Board of India established under section 18.

title: Definition - Child
clause_text: "child" means an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
plain_english_summary: Defines child as any individual below 18 years of age.

title: Definition - Consent Manager
clause_text: "Consent Manager" means a person registered with the Board, who acts as a single point of contact to enable a Data Principal to give, manage, review and withdraw her consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform.
plain_english_summary: Defines Consent Manager as a Board-registered person enabling Data Principals to manage consent.

title: Definition - Data Fiduciary
clause_text: "Data Fiduciary" means any person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing of personal data.
plain_english_summary: Defines Data Fiduciary as the entity that determines purpose and means of processing personal data.

title: Definition - Data Principal
clause_text: "Data Principal" means the individual to whom the personal data relates and where such individual is— (i) a child, includes the parents or lawful guardian of such a child; (ii) a person with disability, includes her lawful guardian, acting on her behalf.
plain_english_summary: Defines Data Principal as the individual whose personal data is processed, including guardians for children and persons with disability.

title: Definition - Data Processor
clause_text: "Data Processor" means any person who processes personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary.
plain_english_summary: Defines Data Processor as anyone processing personal data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary.

title: Definition - Personal Data
clause_text: "personal data" means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data.
plain_english_summary: Defines personal data as any data relating to an identifiable individual.

title: Definition - Personal Data Breach
clause_text: "personal data breach" means any unauthorised processing of personal data or accidental disclosure, acquisition, sharing, use, alteration, destruction or loss of access to personal data, that compromises the confidentiality, integrity or availability of personal data.
plain_english_summary: Defines personal data breach as any unauthorised or accidental act compromising confidentiality, integrity, or availability of personal data.

title: Definition - Significant Data Fiduciary
clause_text: "Significant Data Fiduciary" means any Data Fiduciary or class of Data Fiduciaries as may be notified by the Central Government under section 10.
plain_english_summary: Defines Significant Data Fiduciary as a Data Fiduciary notified as such by the Central Government under section 10.

title: Application - Territorial Scope within India
clause_text: Apply to the processing of digital personal data within the territory of India where the personal data is collected in digital form or in non-digital form and digitised subsequently.
plain_english_summary: The Act applies to processing of digital personal data collected within India, in digital or subsequently digitised form.

title: Application - Extra-territorial Scope
clause_text: Also apply to processing of digital personal data outside the territory of India, if such processing is in connection with any activity related to offering of goods or services to Data Principals within the territory of India.
plain_english_summary: The Act applies extra-territorially when processing relates to offering goods or services to Data Principals in India.

title: Application - Exclusions
clause_text: Not apply to personal data processed by an individual for any personal or domestic purpose; and personal data that is made or caused to be made publicly available by the Data Principal or any person obligated by law to make such personal data publicly available.
plain_english_summary: The Act excludes personal or domestic processing and publicly available personal data from its scope.

title: Grounds for Processing Personal Data
clause_text: A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given her consent or for certain legitimate uses.
plain_english_summary: Personal data may only be processed lawfully, with Data Principal consent or for legitimate uses.

title: Notice - Pre-Consent Requirements
clause_text: Every request made to a Data Principal under section 6 for consent shall be accompanied or preceded by a notice given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal informing her the personal data and purpose of processing, manner to exercise rights, and manner to make complaint to the Board.
plain_english_summary: Every consent request must be preceded or accompanied by a notice informing the Data Principal of data, purpose, rights, and complaint mechanism.

title: Notice - Pre-Commencement Consent
clause_text: Where a Data Principal has given her consent for the processing of her personal data before the date of commencement of this Act, the Data Fiduciary shall, as soon as it is reasonably practicable, give to the Data Principal a notice and may continue to process until consent is withdrawn.
plain_english_summary: For pre-commencement consent, Data Fiduciaries must issue a notice as soon as practicable and may continue processing until consent is withdrawn.

title: Notice - Language Accessibility
clause_text: The Data Fiduciary shall give the Data Principal the option to access the contents of the notice in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
plain_english_summary: Notices must be accessible in English or any Eighth Schedule language of the Constitution.

title: Consent - Requirements
clause_text: The consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, limited to personal data necessary for the specified purpose.
plain_english_summary: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous, and limited to data necessary for the specified purpose.

title: Consent - Invalidity of Non-Compliant Consent
clause_text: Any part of consent which constitutes an infringement of the provisions of this Act or any other law shall be invalid to the extent of such infringement.
plain_english_summary: Any portion of consent that violates this Act or other laws is invalid to the extent of that violation.

title: Consent - Plain Language and DPO Contact
clause_text: Every request for consent shall be presented in clear and plain language, in English or any Eighth Schedule language, and shall provide contact details of the Data Protection Officer or authorised person.
plain_english_summary: Consent requests must be in plain language, available in scheduled languages, and include DPO or authorised contact details.

title: Consent - Right to Withdraw
clause_text: Where consent given by the Data Principal is the basis of processing, the Data Principal shall have the right to withdraw her consent at any time, with the ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which such consent was given.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals can withdraw consent at any time, as easily as it was given.

title: Consent - Consequences of Withdrawal
clause_text: The consequences of withdrawal shall be borne by the Data Principal, and such withdrawal shall not affect the legality of processing before its withdrawal.
plain_english_summary: Withdrawal of consent does not invalidate prior processing; the Data Principal bears the consequences of withdrawal.

title: Consent - Cessation of Processing Post-Withdrawal
clause_text: If a Data Principal withdraws consent, the Data Fiduciary shall, within a reasonable time, cease and cause its Data Processors to cease processing the personal data unless processing is required or authorised under the Act or any other law.
plain_english_summary: On consent withdrawal, the Data Fiduciary and its Data Processors must stop processing within a reasonable time, unless legally authorised to continue.

title: Consent - Via Consent Manager
clause_text: The Data Principal may give, manage, review or withdraw her consent to the Data Fiduciary through a Consent Manager.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals may use a Consent Manager to manage their consent with Data Fiduciaries.

title: Consent Manager - Accountability
clause_text: The Consent Manager shall be accountable to the Data Principal and shall act on her behalf in such manner and subject to such obligations as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: A Consent Manager is accountable to the Data Principal and must act on their behalf as prescribed.

title: Consent Manager - Registration
clause_text: Every Consent Manager shall be registered with the Board in such manner and subject to such technical, operational, financial and other conditions as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: All Consent Managers must register with the Board under prescribed conditions.

title: Consent - Burden of Proof
clause_text: Where a question of consent arises in a proceeding, the Data Fiduciary shall be obliged to prove that a notice was given and consent was given by the Data Principal in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: The burden of proving valid notice and consent lies with the Data Fiduciary in any proceeding.

title: Certain Legitimate Uses
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary may process personal data for legitimate uses including: voluntary provision by Data Principal, State functions, legal obligations, court orders, medical emergencies, public health, disaster management, and employment purposes.
plain_english_summary: Lists specific legitimate purposes for processing personal data without explicit consent, including State functions, legal obligations, medical emergencies, and employment.

title: General Obligations - Data Fiduciary Responsibility
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or failure of a Data Principal to carry out duties, be responsible for complying with this Act in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries remain responsible for compliance regardless of contrary agreements or Data Principal failures.

title: General Obligations - Data Processor Contract
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary may engage a Data Processor to process personal data on its behalf only under a valid contract.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries may only engage Data Processors under a valid contract.

title: General Obligations - Data Accuracy
clause_text: Where personal data is likely to be used to make a decision affecting the Data Principal or disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, the Data Fiduciary shall ensure its completeness, accuracy and consistency.
plain_english_summary: Data used for decisions or shared with other Data Fiduciaries must be complete, accurate, and consistent.

title: General Obligations - Technical and Organisational Measures
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the provisions of this Act.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to comply with the Act.

title: General Obligations - Security Safeguards
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches.

title: General Obligations - Breach Notification
clause_text: In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must notify the Board and all affected Data Principals in the event of a personal data breach.

title: General Obligations - Data Erasure
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law, erase personal data upon consent withdrawal or when the specified purpose is no longer served, and cause its Data Processor to erase such data.
plain_english_summary: Data must be erased when consent is withdrawn or purpose is served, and Data Processors must also erase it, unless law requires retention.

title: General Obligations - Deemed Purpose Completion
clause_text: The purpose shall be deemed to no longer be served if the Data Principal does not approach the Data Fiduciary for the performance of the specified purpose and does not exercise any rights for such time period as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: A purpose is deemed complete if the Data Principal is inactive for a prescribed period.

title: General Obligations - Publishing DPO Contact
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall publish the business contact information of a Data Protection Officer, if applicable, or a person able to answer questions raised by the Data Principal about the processing of her personal data.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must publicly publish contact details of the DPO or designated representative.

title: General Obligations - Grievance Redressal Mechanism
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall establish an effective mechanism to redress the grievances of Data Principals.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must establish an effective grievance redressal mechanism for Data Principals.

title: Processing Children's Data - Parental Consent
clause_text: The Data Fiduciary shall, before processing any personal data of a child or a person with disability who has a lawful guardian, obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must obtain verifiable parental or guardian consent before processing children's data.

title: Processing Children's Data - No Detrimental Processing
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake such processing of personal data that is likely to cause any detrimental effect on the well-being of a child.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries are prohibited from processing children's data in ways likely to harm their well-being.

title: Processing Children's Data - No Tracking or Targeted Advertising
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children.
plain_english_summary: Tracking, behavioural monitoring, and targeted advertising directed at children are prohibited.

title: Processing Children's Data - Exemptions
clause_text: The provisions of sub-sections (1) and (3) shall not be applicable to processing of personal data of a child by such classes of Data Fiduciaries or for such purposes and conditions as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Certain Data Fiduciaries or purposes may be exempted by prescription from children's data obligations under sections 9(1) and 9(3).

title: Significant Data Fiduciary - Designation Criteria
clause_text: The Central Government may notify any Data Fiduciary as Significant Data Fiduciary based on volume and sensitivity of data, risk to Data Principal rights, impact on sovereignty and integrity of India, risk to electoral democracy, security of State, and public order.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government may designate Data Fiduciaries as Significant based on data volume, sensitivity, and risk factors.

title: Significant Data Fiduciary - Additional Obligations
clause_text: The Significant Data Fiduciary shall appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India, appoint an independent data auditor, and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and audits.
plain_english_summary: Significant Data Fiduciaries must appoint an India-based DPO, independent data auditor, and conduct periodic DPIAs and audits.

title: Right to Access Information About Personal Data
clause_text: The Data Principal shall have the right to obtain from the Data Fiduciary a summary of personal data being processed, identities of other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors with whom data was shared, and any other prescribed information.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals have the right to access a summary of their processed data and information on who it was shared with.

title: Right to Correction and Erasure
clause_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of her personal data for which she has previously given consent.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals have the right to correct, complete, update, or erase their personal data.

title: Right to Correction - Data Fiduciary Obligations
clause_text: A Data Fiduciary shall, upon receiving a request for correction, completion or updating from a Data Principal, correct the inaccurate personal data, complete the incomplete personal data, and update the personal data.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries must correct, complete, and update personal data on request from the Data Principal.

title: Right to Erasure - Request Process
clause_text: A Data Principal shall make a request to the Data Fiduciary for erasure of her personal data, and upon receipt, the Data Fiduciary shall erase the data unless retention is necessary for the specified purpose or compliance with any law.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals may request erasure and Data Fiduciaries must comply unless legal retention is required.

title: Right to Grievance Redressal
clause_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to have readily available means of grievance redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager in respect of any act or omission regarding the performance of obligations or exercise of rights under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals have a right to readily accessible grievance redressal from Data Fiduciaries or Consent Managers.

title: Grievance Redressal - Response Timeline
clause_text: The Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager shall respond to any grievances within such period as may be prescribed from the date of its receipt.
plain_english_summary: Data Fiduciaries and Consent Managers must respond to grievances within the prescribed period.

title: Grievance Redressal - Exhaustion Before Board
clause_text: The Data Principal shall exhaust the opportunity of redressing her grievance under this section before approaching the Board.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals must exhaust grievance redressal mechanisms before approaching the Board.

title: Right to Nominate
clause_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to nominate any other individual who shall, in the event of death or incapacity of the Data Principal, exercise the rights of the Data Principal.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals may nominate someone to exercise their data rights in case of death or incapacity.

title: Duties of Data Principal
clause_text: A Data Principal shall comply with applicable laws, not impersonate another person, not suppress material information when providing personal data to State bodies, not register false or frivolous grievances, and furnish only verifiably authentic information for correction or erasure.
plain_english_summary: Data Principals must comply with laws, avoid impersonation, not suppress information, avoid false grievances, and provide authentic information.

title: Cross-Border Transfer - Restriction Power
clause_text: The Central Government may, by notification, restrict the transfer of personal data by a Data Fiduciary for processing to such country or territory outside India as may be so notified.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government may restrict data transfers to specific countries by notification.

title: Cross-Border Transfer - Existing Laws Prevail
clause_text: Nothing in this section shall restrict the applicability of any law for the time being in force that provides for a higher degree of protection for or restriction on transfer of personal data outside India.
plain_english_summary: Any existing law providing higher protection for cross-border data transfers continues to apply.

title: Exemptions - General Grounds
clause_text: The provisions of Chapter II and III and section 16 shall not apply where processing is necessary for enforcing legal rights, by courts or tribunals, for prevention or investigation of offences, for offshore contracts, for corporate restructuring, or for financial default ascertainment.
plain_english_summary: Key Chapter II and III obligations do not apply in legal proceedings, law enforcement, offshore processing, corporate restructuring, and loan default contexts.

title: Exemptions - State and Research
clause_text: The Act shall not apply to processing by notified State instrumentalities for sovereignty, security, and public order; and to processing for research, archiving or statistical purposes where not used for individual decisions.
plain_english_summary: The Act does not apply to State security processing or research and statistical processing not used for individual decisions.

title: Exemptions - Startup Notification
clause_text: The Central Government may notify certain Data Fiduciaries including startups as exempt from the provisions of section 5, sub-sections (3) and (7) of section 8, and sections 10 and 11.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government may exempt startups and certain Data Fiduciaries from notice, data quality, SDF, and access obligations.

title: Establishment of Data Protection Board of India
clause_text: With effect from such date as the Central Government may appoint, there shall be established a Board to be called the Data Protection Board of India.
plain_english_summary: The Central Government shall establish the Data Protection Board of India.

title: Powers and Functions of Board
clause_text: The Board shall inquire into personal data breaches, breaches of Data Fiduciary obligations, Consent Manager breaches, and intermediary violations, and impose penalties as provided in this Act.
plain_english_summary: The Board is empowered to inquire into breaches and impose penalties.

title: Appeal to Appellate Tribunal
clause_text: Any person aggrieved by an order or direction made by the Board under this Act may prefer an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: Any aggrieved person may appeal a Board order to the Appellate Tribunal.

title: Appeal - Time Limit and Form
clause_text: Every appeal shall be filed within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order or direction appealed against, in such form and manner and accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Appeals must be filed within 60 days of receiving the Board's order.

title: Penalties - Imposition
clause_text: If the Board determines on conclusion of an inquiry that breach of the provisions of this Act by a person is significant, it may, after giving the person an opportunity of being heard, impose such monetary penalty specified in the Schedule.
plain_english_summary: The Board may impose monetary penalties from the Schedule after inquiry and hearing.

title: Penalties - Determining Factors
clause_text: While determining the monetary penalty, the Board shall have regard to nature, gravity and duration of breach, type of personal data affected, repetitive nature, gain or loss avoided, mitigation action, proportionality, and likely impact on the person.
plain_english_summary: The Board must consider severity, data type, recurrence, financial gain, mitigation, proportionality, and impact when determining penalties.

title: Penalty - Failure to Implement Security Safeguards
clause_text: Breach in observing the obligation of Data Fiduciary to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach under sub-section (5) of section 8. Penalty: May extend to two hundred and fifty crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Failure to implement reasonable security safeguards may attract a penalty up to Rs 250 crore.

title: Penalty - Failure to Notify Breach
clause_text: Breach in observing the obligation to give the Board or affected Data Principal notice of a personal data breach under sub-section (6) of section 8. Penalty: May extend to two hundred crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Failure to notify a data breach to the Board or affected Data Principals may attract a penalty up to Rs 200 crore.

title: Penalty - Breach of Children's Data Obligations
clause_text: Breach in observance of additional obligations in relation to children under section 9. Penalty: May extend to two hundred crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Breach of children's data obligations under section 9 may attract a penalty up to Rs 200 crore.

title: Penalty - Breach of Significant Data Fiduciary Obligations
clause_text: Breach in observance of additional obligations of Significant Data Fiduciary under section 10. Penalty: May extend to one hundred and fifty crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Failure to comply with SDF obligations under section 10 may attract a penalty up to Rs 150 crore.

title: Penalty - Breach of Data Principal Duties
clause_text: Breach in observance of the duties under section 15. Penalty: May extend to ten thousand rupees.
plain_english_summary: Breach of a Data Principal's duties under section 15 may attract a penalty up to Rs 10,000.

title: Penalty - Breach of Voluntary Undertaking
clause_text: Breach of any term of voluntary undertaking accepted by the Board under section 32. Penalty: Up to the extent applicable for the breach in respect of which the proceedings under section 28 were instituted.
plain_english_summary: Breaching a voluntary undertaking attracts a penalty equivalent to the maximum for the underlying breach.

title: Penalty - Breach of Other Provisions
clause_text: Breach of any other provision of this Act or the rules made thereunder. Penalty: May extend to fifty crore rupees.
plain_english_summary: Breach of any other provision of the DPDP Act not specifically listed in the Schedule may attract a penalty up to Rs 50 crore.
